services.caveat: Windows OpenSSH Server on Omar PC (step 12 of OMAR-REMOTE-CONTROL.md); firewall rule Aphrody-SSH-In-Tunnel admits 10.200.77.0/24 on 10.200.77.10 only; authorized keys: owner (GitHub aphrody-dev and aphrody-owner-pc) and aphrody-vps-to-omar-pc.

Native OpenSSH of Omar's WSL2 Ubuntu (owner note 2026-10-09). Port 22 stays the Windows OpenSSH Server; WSL sshd listens on 2222 (sshd_config.d/60-aphrody-wsl.conf). WSL networkingMode=mirrored makes it a 10.200.77.10 listener through the Windows wg1 adapter; NAT mode needs netsh portproxy 10.200.77.10:2222 to the WSL address, refreshed at logon. WSL runs no WireGuard of its own (the Windows tunnel owns the omar key). Same authorized keys as ssh-omar, LF endings, ~/.ssh 700 and authorized_keys 600.

Private WireGuard socket-proxyd reaches the canonical loopback MCP listener. /mcp requires APHRODY_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN from its protected host store; no public listener. Tool capabilities are verified from the deployed binary.

firewall.note: Rules carry the aphrody-wg-<peer> comment. scripts/ops/admin-access.ts of Shenron only deletes rules whose comment is shenron-admin, so the two never collide. The tunnel subnet is RFC 1918 outside 10.8.0.0/24: admin-access-host.ts skips it (no ufw, fail2ban, pg_hba or admin-IP entry). meshDenied: dbfr hosts PostgreSQL and Redis, so it is reached per declared port only, never through a mesh.
